title: Counterexamples to the multicolor nonnested matching conjecture
summary: We show that excluding nested pairs can increase the number of vertices needed to force a matching of one color, disproving a conjecture of Barát, Gyárfás and Tóth. A matching consists of edges with no shared endpoint. In a fixed vertex order, two edges are nested if both endpoints of one lie between those of the other. For $r$ colors and a target of $k$ edges, the classical theorem guarantees a matching of one color on $(r-1)(k-1)+2k$ vertices when every pair is joined by an edge.
